title: Japanese Art of Ikebana Draws Those Seeking Calm
paragraphs: Ikebana, the Japanese art of flower arranging, has a history of more than 500 years. Today, it continues to attract not only people interested in tradition, but also newcomers who are looking for a sense of calm in their busy lives.

The oldest of the three major schools of ikebana is Ikenobo, which is based in Kyoto. The school has its roots in Buddhism and now has groups around the world. In its traditional style, flowers, leaves and branches are arranged to look the way they might appear in nature. The arrangements have three main parts. The tallest, called "shin," represents a person's core. The second, "soe," is placed at the side and expresses individuality. The third, "tai," often a flower or fresh leaves, represents the future.

For many people, ikebana is much more than simply arranging flowers. Hiroyuki Okada, 40, began taking lessons about seven years ago and now teaches the Ikenobo style. Okada described the practice as having a purifying and healing effect, like a "detox," and said it helps people come face to face with themselves. According to Okada, the feel of the petals and leaves is very important, and can be compared to petting a kitten or a puppy.

Mayu Shimizu, who has taken lessons from Okada for about three years, said ikebana has a healing effect similar to yoga or meditation. Shimizu explained that it brings a "moment of nothingness" that leaves the mind clearer.

Senko Ikenobo, who is expected to become the next head of the Ikenobo school, said ikebana is about the relationship between the creator and the flowers. She has seen it help women who are balancing work and motherhood, or caring for their aging parents.

Science may support these experiences. According to Jeannette Haviland-Jones, a professor of social psychology at Rutgers University in the US, studies show that flowers and their scents can make people happier.
Ikebana students include people of all ages, from small children copying their mothers to people over 100 years old.
